toolCalls.name: StructuredOutput

output.brief:
The drafted claim should not go out as written. The platform's audit trail shows the architect answered 62 of 64 information requests within the contract period. The median was 4 working days. The two late ones were minor finishes queries that Callerby itself marked as having no programme impact. Of the 41 requests the claim calls late, 39 sat in Callerby's own draft status for 9–47 days before being submitted. The structural query on CO-09 was answered in 4 days.

The change orders were mostly small interior items. CO-09, the MRI move, was issued on 6 November. The crane left in October, before CO-09 existed. Callerby's own report called the crane's removal a cost-saving measure. The superintendent says the steel was on site and the crane and frame crew went to Kestrel. The most likely main cause is Callerby moving the crane and crew, with possibly some genuine CO-09 delay. I'm not certain how much CO-09 contributed.

Next steps: hold the 1 December submission. Commission an independent delay analysis, and have it test any CO-09 time claim separately. Check the Fenmore fee incentive. Do not discipline the superintendent. Review how crane transfers between projects are approved before blaming the incentive scheme.
